ambiguities.description: Is Contact identified by anything beyond the Vendor+Region combination (e.g. does Contact have its own contact_id, or is the vendor-region pair itself the sole key with name/email/phone as pure attributes)? The transcript describes contact by name/email/phone but never gives an explicit identifier for the Contact entity itself; the reference_mode 'contact_id' was invented for modeling purposes and is not confirmed by the transcript.

ambiguities.description: Should RiskReview have an explicit 'is_current'/'signed_off' status attribute modeled? The conversation clarifies that a vendor accumulates many reviews but only one is 'current' and 'signed-off' -- this distinction (current vs historical, signed-off vs not) is referenced but no field name or value set was given, so it could not be modeled as a proper attribute/constraint beyond a general frequency note.

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle... But one of them is the current signed-off one.
A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: TaxId is explicitly stated to be non-unique (duplicates and shared parent filings exist), yet it is still recorded as an attribute of Vendor. Should TaxId perhaps be modeled at a different grain (e.g., a separate 'Legal Entity' concept) given the duplicate/parent-subsidiary issue flagged by both Dana and Raj as an ongoing compliance and cleanup problem? This was explicitly called out of scope but flagged here as a modeling risk.

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
The duplicates are also a compliance problem, for what it's worth. If we've got the same entity twice we can't see aggregate exposure.

ambiguities.description: The three vendor addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) are mentioned but never modeled in detail -- granularity and structure of Address (single text value vs structured street/city/state/postal, and whether each address type is a separate fact type) is unresolved and was not incorporated into the model due to insufficient detail.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: The naming collision between 'spend tier' and 'risk tier' (both casually called 'tier') is a terminology/overloaded-term issue: stakeholders acknowledge people still use the ambiguous single word 'tier' in conversation despite two distinct system fields existing. This is a communication/process risk beyond the data model itself.

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." -- We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does.

ambiguities.description: What happens to in-flight Purchase Orders when a Vendor is suspended (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a steering group/Legal decision. No constraint or additional status was modeled for this, per the facilitator's explicit parking of the issue.

source_references.excerpt: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag mentioned by Mei (an informal spreadsheet column indicating preference when multiple vendors can supply the same item) was explicitly identified as ad hoc with no defined rule, and per facilitator's decision was excluded from the model. Flagging for completeness in case business later formalizes this rule.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere.
It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Temporal/historical tracking: Vendor status, spend tier, and risk tier appear to be current-state fields (each vendor has exactly one value at a time), but the transcript doesn't clarify whether history of status/tier changes needs to be tracked (unlike RiskReview which explicitly keeps historical records). This may be a gap if audit trail of status/tier changes is required.
